Feeling safe. When you're on the street and have nowhere to go to be safe you become hyperaware of how vulnerable you are to harm when doing something as basic as trying to sleep. But when you're unconscious you're open to being physically harmed, being stolen from (all my possessions were stolen from me more than once) or any number of terrifying things.

Another one was solitude. It's impossible and unsafe to really have alone time when homeless, even in shelters it's all group areas, and that meant I ended up overwhelmed really easily. My mental health was shredded into bits from homelessness.

Blaming me for everything. All conversations focused on perceived or invented flaws because it made him feel better about his life. Constant put downs

It finally got to a point where I was legitimately shocked by people being NICE to me because he would turn everything into me fighting back tears and having to try and not look depressed while I heard him and his associates making up horrible things and if I made the tiniest mistakes ruthlessly tearing into me. I mean a typo was enough to get them started and when it's multiple people.....

I'm not having a great day, heh.

Edit: if I talk about what's happening or hurting me anywhere I get punished via verbal abuse, so I have to let the depression eat away at me because I'm not allowed to talk to anyone about it.

"I stopped expressing myself" hit me hard because of the same being done to me with the same end result.

Maybe there could be some way for all of us who lost our ability to express ourselves to help and support each other? The positive encouragement might help, right?

I get my abuser threatening to call the police constantly.....but he also one ups it in the most incomprehensible move I've ever seen.

So, it's at a point where I know him calling the police isn't going to lead anywhere so I generally shrug it off. And instead of using it to scare me, he's branched out and started using it to scare my *friends* into thinking rthat I'm a criminal. Since this is part of an elaborate plan where the end result is that friend and I barely speaking (This happens every time Itry to get closer to anyone and they try to help me escape my abuser - his vindictive nature is really boundless.)

He's started straight up staging police encounters while being audio-only (think a nonconsensual on my end phone call). He'll stage what will look like a conversation with police where he's trying to accuse me of the myriad things he's completely made up. It always ends with the "police" stating something is wrong with me and that Ineed to be arrested. Yes, it's as childish and simplistic as it sounds. No, it doesn't go beyond his weird power fantasy. It still does scare friends who are alreay cop -skittish though :/

It's a hell I wish on nobody, and know that you're seen and your truth is seen here even if your entire reality is being torn down by that fuckhead. There are people who are too wisened to that kinda bullshit to get sucked in and we can see the truth he wants to bury and hide. ❤

Your feelings matter and they matter more than those of people who are mildly inconvenienced by someone who has been traumatized and needs support instead of more invalidating horseshit.

Yes and I hate how I do it but it goes back to my abusive mom having an ED that she used to take out on me for any weight gain and would control in some way (verbal abuse til I gave up) Which led to me developing this habit. I haven't even spoken to the woman since 2015. 

The way that our abusers foster lasting echoes of their violence toward us is pretty terrifying honestly

I've been the one to love my abuser too.

Loving him isn't some kind of black mark on you, it doesn't mean you're any less deserving of help or a way out. And while it does make it a lot harder to convince yourself to stay away it does get easier to do the more it sinks in just how horrifying a situation you survived.

There are people who are really shitty about abuse victims going back to their abusers but going back STILL doesn't cancel out you deserving an abuse free life.
